overall_summary: Soft CPI data is crushing Fed hike odds and driving Bitcoin toward sixty-five thousand with strong ETF inflows and long-term holder strength. Macro tailwinds like falling yields and a softer dollar support risk assets. Geopolitical risks around Iran and sanctions remain a potential volatility source but are secondary for now.
key_points: Soft CPI crushes Fed hike odds, lifts Bitcoin
Spot ETFs flip to one hundred eighty-one million inflows
Long-term holder dominance hits thirty-month high
Yields and dollar drop on cool inflation data
Iran energy threats and sanctions add risk

items.title: Bitcoin Nears $65K as Soft CPI Crushes Fed Hike Odds
items.summary: June US CPI came in at 3.5 percent year-over-year, well below the 3.8 percent expected, with a 0.4 percent monthly drop. Core was also softer. This slashed July Fed rate-hike odds from the mid-30s percent range down to teens or lower. Traders should care because it eases the tight-money overhang that had weighed on Bitcoin amid Iran tensions, opening the door for risk-asset recovery if oil prices stay in check.
items.impact: Supports near-term upside as rate-cut hopes rebuild

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Flip to $181M Inflows After Outflows
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about 181 million dollars in net inflows on Tuesday after the prior session saw roughly 425 million in redemptions. BlackRock's IBIT drove most of the buying, and Ether ETFs also turned positive. This matters for traders because it signals institutions stepping back in on the CPI bounce, providing real demand that can help sustain any rally beyond short covering.
items.impact: Positive flow momentum aids price support

items.title: Strategy CEO Outlines Path to Resume Bitcoin Buying
items.summary: Strategy Inc. CEO Phong Le detailed a plan to rebuild cash reserves, normalize its preferred stock trading near par, and then resume Bitcoin accumulation toward a one-million-coin target. He personally bought a million dollars of the preferred shares. Traders care because this is the largest corporate holder signaling a return to net buying after recent liquidity sales, potentially adding meaningful demand.

items.title: Bitcoin Long-Term Holder Dominance Hits 30-Month High
items.summary: The share of Bitcoin held by long-term holders versus short-term ones reached a 30-month peak on CryptoQuant data. This shows strong hands continuing to accumulate or hold through volatility. For traders it reduces the pool of likely sellers and often appears near accumulation phases, making sustained upside more plausible if macro stays supportive.
items.impact: Tighter circulating supply supports higher prices

items.title: Wrapped Bitcoin Exchange Outflows Hit Six-Week High
items.summary: About 326 WBTC left exchanges in a single day, the largest net outflow since early June according to Santiment. Fewer coins sitting on trading platforms means less immediate sell pressure. Traders should note this classic bullish on-chain signal during the rebound, as it suggests holders are securing coins rather than preparing to dump into strength.
items.impact: Reduced available supply can amplify upside moves

items.title: Senate Democrats Slam Clarity Act as Corrupt Over Trump Ties
items.summary: Senators Murphy, Van Hollen and Merkley publicly opposed the crypto market-structure bill, calling it corrupt unless it fully severs President Trump's personal crypto interests with strict ethics rules. The bill already faces a tight timeline before summer recess. Traders watch this because bipartisan support is needed for passage, and fresh Democratic resistance raises the odds of further delay in clear regulatory rules for the industry.
items.impact: Adds uncertainty to near-term regulatory progress

items.title: Cooler June CPI Beats Forecasts, Eases Hike Odds
items.summary: June CPI dropped 0.4 percent month over month, the biggest fall since April 2020, bringing the annual rate to 3.5 percent versus the 3.8 percent expected. Core CPI was flat on the month and rose just 2.6 percent year over year, cooler than forecasts. Energy prices, especially gasoline, drove much of the relief after a temporary ceasefire, though oil has since climbed again. Traders should care because this soft print reduced near-term rate-hike bets, lifted stocks and crypto, and pulled Treasury yields lower, creating a more risk-on backdrop ahead of today's PPI.
items.impact: Supports risk assets and crypto via lower rate-hike odds in near term

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh Testifies, Pledges Inflation Fight
items.summary: New Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his first congressional testimony yesterday to the House Financial Services Committee on the semiannual Monetary Policy Report, reaffirming commitment to bring inflation sustainably lower with no tolerance for persistently elevated prices. He stressed policy independence and vowed to do his job even under political pressure, without giving explicit signals on the next rate move. A Senate appearance is also on the calendar. Crypto traders should watch closely because his tone shapes rate-path expectations that drive liquidity and Bitcoin valuations.
items.impact: Keeps policy uncertainty high until clearer rate guidance emerges

items.title: June PPI Due Today After Soft CPI Print
items.summary: The Producer Price Index for June is scheduled for release this morning at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, with markets expecting a soft headline near zero month over month after May's 1.1 percent jump, driven by earlier energy relief. Core PPI is watched for stickiness and is projected around 0.4 percent. This follows yesterday's cooler CPI and comes as oil prices have rebounded on renewed Iran tensions. Traders care because a hot PPI could rekindle inflation fears and reverse the risk-on move, while a soft one would reinforce the disinflation narrative for rates and Bitcoin.
items.impact: Could confirm or reverse the post-CPI risk-on move depending on core reading

items.title: Treasury Yields Drop Sharply on Soft CPI Data
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields fell noticeably after the cooler-than-expected June CPI, with the two-year note dropping more than seven basis points and the ten-year sliding over two basis points. This reversed some of the prior hike-scare rally that had pushed the two-year to multi-month highs. Yields are slightly firmer in early trading today. Bond moves matter for crypto because lower yields ease financial conditions and support risk assets, while any rebound tied to hot PPI or oil could pressure Bitcoin.
items.impact: Easier financial conditions supportive for equities and crypto

items.title: Empire State Manufacturing Index and Beige Book Due
items.summary: The New York Fed's Empire State Manufacturing Index for July is released today alongside PPI, after June's reading of 5.7. The Fed's Beige Book, summarizing regional economic conditions, is also due later today. These provide timely signals on manufacturing strength, price pressures, and overall activity heading into the late-July FOMC. Traders should monitor them for clues on growth and inflation persistence that influence rate expectations and dollar direction.
items.impact: Growth and inflation signals that can shift rate-path pricing

items.title: Dollar Softens as Soft CPI Cuts Hike Bets
items.summary: The U.S. dollar index eased after the cooler CPI print reduced immediate rate-hike odds, with the greenback at multi-week lows against some majors in the reaction. Geopolitical oil spikes and upcoming data keep volatility high. A weaker dollar has historically been supportive for Bitcoin and commodities. Watch DXY closely around today's PPI and Fed speak, as any rebound on sticky producer prices could reverse the recent relief.
items.impact: Weaker dollar generally constructive for crypto and risk assets

items.title: US Reimposes Iran Naval Blockade Amid Ongoing Strikes
items.summary: The United States has reinstated its naval blockade of Iranian ports and launched another round of strikes on Iranian military targets for the fourth consecutive night. Iran has retaliated by hitting commercial tankers and US assets in the region, including in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. Oil prices have jumped sharply on fears of disrupted flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Traders should care because this is a major energy chokepoint, driving higher oil prices, inflation risks, and broad risk-off sentiment that typically pressures Bitcoin and equities.
items.impact: Higher oil prices and risk-off selling pressure on crypto and stocks

items.title: Iran Threatens to Halt All Middle East Energy Exports
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard has threatened to stop all oil and gas exports from the Middle East, saying they will be for everyone or no one, in response to the US blockade. This comes as shipping traffic through Hormuz has already plummeted. For traders, this is a black-swan style energy shock risk that could send oil soaring further and fuel global inflation fears. Expect increased volatility across commodities, currencies, and risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Potential severe oil supply shock and risk-off market reaction

items.title: US Unveils Revised Russia Sanctions Bill Targeting China and India
items.summary: US senators have released an updated bipartisan Russia sanctions bill, backed in spirit by the late Lindsey Graham, that would allow tariffs of up to 100 percent on the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas, primarily China and India. The bill also hits Russian officials, banks, and energy projects, with waiver power for the president. This matters for markets because secondary tariffs could escalate trade tensions with major economies and disrupt energy flows, adding another layer of geopolitical risk.
items.impact: Heightened trade tensions and potential secondary sanctions pressure on global energy markets

items.title: China Q2 GDP Growth Slows to 4.3 Percent, Misses Target
items.summary: China reported second-quarter GDP growth of 4.3 percent, the weakest in over three years and below the lower end of its full-year target, with officials and analysts linking some weakness to global trade disruptions from the Iran conflict. Weak domestic demand and investment also weighed. Crypto traders should watch this because a slowing Chinese economy signals softer global growth, which can reduce risk appetite and commodity demand, often weighing on Bitcoin.
items.impact: Weaker global growth outlook reducing risk appetite

items.title: US Freezes Over 130 Million in Iran-Linked Cryptocurrency
items.summary: The US Treasury has frozen more than 130 million dollars in cryptocurrency allegedly linked to Iran's central bank and sanctions-evasion networks as part of renewed pressure amid the military escalation. Tether was involved in freezing some of the assets. This is directly relevant for crypto markets as it highlights ongoing government scrutiny of crypto for sanctions busting and could increase regulatory fears or selling pressure on related tokens.
items.impact: Increased crypto regulatory scrutiny and potential liquidity freezes

items.title: Ukraine Intensifies Drone Strikes on Russian Oil and Shipping
items.summary: Ukrainian forces have continued heavy drone attacks on Russian oil refineries, including the last major one previously untouched this year, and dozens of tankers and vessels in the Sea of Azov and Black Sea, forcing shipping suspensions and fuel shortages in Russia. Russia has responded with attacks on Ukrainian ports. This secondary energy disruption adds to global oil market tightness already pressured by the Iran conflict, supporting higher prices and broader inflation concerns.
items.impact: Additional upward pressure on oil prices from Russian supply disruptions
